sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma

items.q: What is the recommended initial management for a patient diagnosed with an asymptomatic pituitary microadenoma?
opts: Wait and watch with repeat MRI in 3 to 6 months
items.exp: For asymptomatic microadenoma, management is wait and watch with repeat MRI after 3-6 months; treat only if size increases. (Book p944)

items.q: What is the first-line medical drug of choice (DOC) for symptomatic prolactinomas and macroadenomas?
items.exp: Cabergoline is the first-line medical drug of choice for prolactinomas. (Book p944)

items.q: Due to its prolonged elimination half-life, cabergoline is typically initiated at a weekly dose of ___ mg twice weekly.
items.exp: Cabergoline has an increased half-life allowing weekly dosing at 0.25 mg twice weekly. (Book p944)

items.q: Which is NOT a recognized acute adverse effect of dopamine agonists such as cabergoline?
items.exp: Dopamine agonists cause nausea, vomiting, postural hypotension, and dizziness, rather than severe hypertension. (Book p944)

items.q: At cumulative cabergoline doses exceeding 2 g/week, what major cardiopulmonary toxicities can occur?
items.exp: Cumulative cabergoline > 2 g/week (or high doses) can cause tricuspid regurgitation (valvulopathy) and lung fibrosis. (Book p944)

items.q: What proportion of prolactinoma patients exhibit dopamine agonist resistance to cabergoline?
items.exp: Dopamine agonist resistance to cabergoline occurs in 20% of patients. (Book p944)

items.q: A 28-year-old woman with a microprolactinoma desires pregnancy. Which dopamine agonist is preferred because of its extensive safety record in gestation?
items.exp: Bromocriptine is used in pregnancy due to extensive historical safety data. (Book p944)

items.q: If a woman taking bromocriptine during pregnancy intends to breastfeed after delivery, when should the drug be discontinued?
opts: Stop at onset of active labor
items.exp: Bromocriptine must be stopped 7 days before lactation to allow prolactin-mediated milk production. (Book p944)

items.q: Match the therapeutic milestone in prolactinoma management to its expected timeframe — 1) Normalization of serum prolactin levels 2) Significant shrinkage of tumor volume … A) Within 4 weeks B) Within 3 to 6 months
items.exp: Prolactin levels normalize within 4 weeks; tumor shrinkage is achieved by 3-6 months. (Book p944)

items.q: Which condition is NOT an established indication for surgical resection of a prolactinoma?
opts: Asymptomatic microadenoma with serum prolactin of 60 ug/L
Persistent visual field defects after 1 month of medical therapy
items.exp: Surgical indications include dopamine agonist resistance, persistent visual defects after 1 month of medical Rx, unstable apoplexy, and pregnancy unresponsive to therapy. (Book p944)

items.q: What immunohistochemical proliferation marker is utilized to evaluate extremely rare malignant prolactinomas?
items.exp: Malignant prolactinoma is very rare and identified by the Ki67 proliferation marker. (Book p944)

items.q: What modality serves as the last resort for patients with refractory prolactinoma who are unfit for surgical resection?
items.exp: Gamma Knife stereotactic radiotherapy is the last resort if the patient is unfit for surgery. (Book p944)

items.q: Assess the primary goals of prolactinoma therapy: I Normalize serum prolactin and restore gonadal axis function. II Induce tumor shrinkage and normalize anterior pituitary function.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Goals of therapy are tumor shrinkage by 3-6 months, prolactin normalization by 4 weeks, pituitary function normalization, and restoration of gonadal function. (Book p944)
